info.title: HyperFlow tenant controls and workspace API
info.description: Phase 11 tenant-operation supplement. Existing business operations remain documented in the application API reference and phase contracts. This is not yet the final whole-product parity inventory.

get.description: Administrator view. Hashes and plaintext credentials are omitted. API-client counts cover admitted scoped requests, excluding Firebase browser sessions and provider charges. With view=lifecycle, requires a current human owner or administrator and returns HyperFlow-owned lifecycle receipts. service=communications reads the separate service. dataset/revision/offset exports 512000-byte base64 chunks at a suspended revision, with whole-dataset and chunk SHA-256 hashes. Credentials and file contents are excluded.

200.description: Authoritative app-owned result; not proof of an external provider effect

post.description: With view=lifecycle, current human owners or administrators may request suspend/resume using requestId and revision. service=communications forwards those commands with a human audit journal and returns the Communications-owned receipt. Without service, only HyperFlow database state changes and enabled runtime guards are required. Suspension independently reads Communications suspension state. erase_database additionally requires confirmation="Erase HyperFlow database records", backupReviewed=true, a recorded export at the current suspended revision, and independently verified Communications status closed. Retry an interrupted erasure with the original requestId; never invent a replacement. Successful erasure is irreversible via Resume. File manifests, identities, membership, recovery audit, provider resources and backups are retained. Communications erasure requires separate authority and is not forwarded by this endpoint. erase_managed_files is a separate human-administrator operation at a suspended or database-erased revision. It requires requestId, revision, confirmation="Erase HyperFlow stored files" and backupReviewed=true; processes25 manifests per request; replay continues the same operation. File receipts, provider backups/versions and unmanaged objects remain.

schema.description: Creation requires requestId/name/secret/expiresAt/scopes. Rotation requires id/secret/expiresAt. Revocation requires id. Budget requires dailyLimit. Revision is the current control ledger revision. Identical creation/rotation replay is safe.

put.description: Replaces the existing workspace snapshot only after tenant and project revision checks. 3.8 MB write limit; 413 when exceeded. Separate operational ledgers are unaffected.

get.description: Read-only status. Optional projectId must belong to current tenant. Returns project, schedules, mailboxes, mailboxStatus (available/unavailable), workspaces, lastRun, lastDigest, scheduler, upgradeRequired, unboundScheduleIds and validationFailures. Does not bind or disable legacy schedules.

Current tenant and files:read for API clients. Without id, returns items/next; default25 and maximum100. Invisible entries still advance pagination. With id returns file; download=1 adds a generation-specific bearer url and expiresAt, valid for60 seconds. Only author sees private files; current members see organization files. Requires active tenant and enabled private storage.

Account changes and disabled storage fail closed. No automatic write retries.

get.description: With view=diagnostics, requires owner/admin and operations:read for API credentials. Writes an access audit before reading up to 100 records per dataset. Returns aggregate statuses only; no private content, credentials or provider error bodies. Unavailable and partial data remain explicit. This is not proof of delivery or a cost/SLA claim. Other views retain the existing operations API.

200.description: Audited bounded observation with auditId, observedAt, organizationId, datasets, scheduler, lifecycle, communications and usage

403.description: Administrator membership or operations scope required

503.description: Access audit unavailable; no diagnostic records read

Bearer.description: Firebase ID token, or scoped hf organization credential. Tenant-control mutations require a human administrator Firebase session.

ManagedFile.description: HyperFlow file metadata. The API omits bucket, object path, session credentials and chunk fingerprints. Administrator cancellation of a private file returns only an ID/state/deletion receipt.
